solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dash off and run off after fabulous lady

parts.note: to dash off a letter is to pen it, writing it quickly
to run off with a lover is to elope

explanation.surface: Someone leaves in a hurry and bolts, chasing after a legendary woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means 'of fable', not 'wonderful': the lady is Odysseus's faithful wife in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus's wife in Homer's Odyssey is a figure of legend, hence a lady out of fable.

definitions.meaning: to run fast, as in rain ... down or a runner ... along
an animal's skin with the fur still on

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: moving at speed, and the furry skin of an animal.

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of Tory
a blunder is an error

explanation.surface: A political commentator fears a gaffe by the head of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the two pieces side by side; 'Tory leader' looks like a politician but gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread and terror are synonyms for intense fear.

parts.note: C is the slang abbreviation for cocaine
to make tracks is to set off, so leaving

explanation.surface: Someone takes cocaine and then heads off, in a seedy little drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts the drug letter ahead of the departure word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaving means splitting apart, so a synonym for cutting.

clue.text: Bond embracing girl? Say it isn't so!

indicators.note: embracing means one word wraps its arms around the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a bond is a binding agreement, a contract
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: Someone hears that James Bond is hugging a woman and refuses to believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' with its capital suggests 007, but it is a binding agreement; DI sits inside, splitting it as CONTRA-DI-CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny what someone says is to tell them it isn't so, which is what contradicting means.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a cosmetic cream or lotion is an oil, as in sun oil

explanation.surface: Someone bashful fusses over a jar of cold cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as a bashful adjective but is a verb, to start back; 'cold cream' is split into C and a word for cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse shies when it jerks back in fright, and recoiling is flinching back the same way.

clue.text: Housing Eastern workers in temporary accomodation

indicators.note: in places the eastern workers inside the canvas shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
men are workers, as in a boss and his men

explanation.surface: A report on eastern labourers lodged in makeshift lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like a verb in the surface but is a noun, a block of dwellings; the clue spells 'accomodation' with one m as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building of rented flats, so a form of housing.

indicators.note: around means the god's name surrounds the letter for Italy

parts.note: the Titans were the elder gods of Greek myth
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An artist's deity is shown circling Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Painter's' stands for 'is': the painter is the god around Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter.

indicators.note: getting means the failed person takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a has-been is a loser, someone past success
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A washed-up actor rambles on after finally winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Looser means less tightly controlled, so more rambling or slack.

indicators.note: say tells you the word for cane is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to cane is to beat

explanation.surface: Sugar cane, it seems, is a source of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sugar cane' reads as one phrase, but 'sugar' ends the definition and 'cane' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is the root crop from which much table sugar is refined.

clue.text: Pulling back trigger ends in recoil

indicators.note: in places the end letters of the gun part inside the word for recoil

parts.note: to recoil is to react, so a reaction

indicators.note: ends picks out the two outermost letters of the word trigger

explanation.surface: Squeezing a gun's trigger results in a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes T and R from trigger, which go inside REACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is a drawing back, as when a claw or a statement is withdrawn.

indicators.note: for the audience means the word for rock is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a boulder is a big rock

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a weightier stone so the crowd can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavier' is meant in the printing sense: bolder type is heavier, thicker type.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold print uses heavier strokes, so bolder type is heavier type.

clue.text: He's ardent, I fancy, showing crush

indicators.note: fancy as a verb to imagine, signalling the letters be rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who thinks himself a passionate lover is shown to be crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' looks like a remark, 'I think', but 'fancy' is the anagram signal, and 'crush' suggests infatuation, though it is a verb, to deflate.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush someone's spirit is to dishearten them, take away their hope.

parts.note: in Nice, France, a friend is ami in French
a guy is a rope or wire holding something steady, a cable

explanation.surface: A pleasant pal, a decent bloke, is good company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the sentence hides its capital: it is the French city, hence a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and good-natured, as in an amicable settlement.

indicators.note: producing means the run of letters is brought out from the words around it

explanation.surface: The Arsenal football team, nicknamed the Gunners, play in Zaragoza and field a replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal, a London football club; the answer sits across 'Gunners at Z'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing, a substitute.

indicators.note: after means the measurement word follows the temperature letter

parts.note: a reading is a measurement taken from an instrument

explanation.surface: A soldier's temperature is taken after a march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like it belongs with 'marching', but it places the measurement after the temperature letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading is walking with deliberate steps, so close to marching.

clue.text: One won't stand for old people!

definitions.text: One won't stand for old people!

parts.words: One won't stand for old people!
parts.note: reads like someone refusing to give up a seat on a bus to the elderly, but 'won't stand for' means will not tolerate: a person prejudiced against the old

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who discriminates against people for being old will not tolerate them.

clue.text: Put on jeans, tucked in sort of shirt

indicators.note: tucked in means the jeans go inside the shirt, held within it

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt, a sort of shirt
Levis are a well-known brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Someone dresses in jeans with a shirt tucked into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' is a broadcaster putting on a show, not dressing; the jeans sit inside the shirt, TE-LEVIS-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To televise a programme is to broadcast it, putting it on air.

indicators.note: opening of means just the first letter of the word security

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone has to break open the lock on a security door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is force or pressure applied, as in engineering stress on a beam.

clue.text: Most musical soprano with very little strain

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in vocal scores
wee is Scottish for very small
a test is a strain or trial, as in testing someone's patience

explanation.surface: A soprano sings with barely any effort, and the result is beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests a musical phrase, fitting the surface, but it means a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetest describes the most pleasing and melodious sound, hence the most musical.

indicators.note: below means, in this down entry, the touching word sits under the desire word

parts.note: to desire is to want
on means touching, in contact with

explanation.surface: A leering remark about wanting to touch someone's lower parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' reads as a smutty hint but places the second piece beneath the first in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton means sexually unrestrained, so lecherous or lewd.

clue.text: Strike time before the French dispute

parts.note: to bat a ball is to strike it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Workers walk out, then argue with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action but means hitting; 'before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight or struggle, so a dispute in the sense of a contest.

definitions.meaning: the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given a donkey's head
a backside or rear, ass being American slang for it

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to the weaver who becomes an ass, and means the behind.

clue.text: Preparing dinner, I get part of recipe

indicators.note: preparing suggests the letters are worked over and made into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook making supper picks up one of the items the recipe lists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preparing' fits the kitchen scene but it is the anagram signal for DINNER I GET.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one item among the components a recipe calls for.

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Someone shows a horrible, cruel longing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the wordplay and also describes the answer, a nasty covetous longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is a resentful longing for what another person has, a vicious form of yearning.

indicators.note: upward means, in this down entry, the word for trend is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tide is a trend, as in the tide of opinion

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a trend is rightly heading up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' looks like an adjective but is a verb, as an editor corrects copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to revise it, putting errors right.

parts.note: sole means single, the only one

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word for male drops out

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A lonely bachelor grows serious as he loses his courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' sounds like despair, but it removes A, the middle of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and serious, very close to earnest.

clue.text: Most callous is sent to stir

indicators.note: stir means the letters are mixed up as if stirred in a pot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The hardest-hearted criminal is sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison, which fits the surface, but here it signals the anagram of IS SENT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoniest means hardest or most unfeeling, as in a stony stare, so most callous.
